messages:
Samir: Heads up — started a partial quant rollout for llama-v2-13b on the dedicated pools. Intent: INT8 kernels for most transformer layers, explicitly exclude embeddings and lm_head, plus per-layer calibration thresholds. Doing canary -> gradual rollout.

Lee: Nice. Any perf measurements from the canary?

Samir: Yup. Short summary: p50 improved but p95 regressed on short-sequence traffic. Suspect kernel selection + batcher interaction + KV cache tagging. Full logs below.

Alex: Can you paste the perf deltas?

Samir: Sure — two snapshots: baseline (fp16 kernels everywhere except quantized endpoints) vs canary (int8 partial):

```
Baseline (FP16) — p50: 48ms, p95: 132ms, throughput: 420 req/s
Canary (INT8 per-layer) — p50: 36ms, p95: 180ms, throughput: 460 req/s
Observed: lower median but heavier tail, concentrated on seq_len <= 24 requests.
```

Morgan: Interesting. So overall throughput up but tail latency worse. That screams batching or cold-path mismatch.

Tariq: Any KV cache anomalies? I remember a similar tail when cache keys weren't variant-tagged.

Samir: Yeah — we saw ~3% increase in KV cache miss rate on canary. Root cause looks like cache key mismatch + eviction churn. When switching kernels we didn't add model_variant to the cache key so quantized + non-quantized requests were sharing entries leading to less effective reuse.

Jen: Oof. That can amplify tail because short seqs rely on prefix caching most.

Samir: Agreed. Also the kernel selector currently picks kernel by model_width and hardware capability only. It doesn't consider (seq_len, batch_size) perf surface. For small sequences, our FP8 microkernel on A100 is actually faster than the INT8 kernel we chose. So selector picked INT8 -> suboptimal for short seq loads.

Alex: Do we have profiling traces that show per-kernel latency across (batch, seq_len)? Would help tune selector heuristics.

Samir: Pasted a snippet from the perf profiler (per-kernel median in ms):

```
kernel: fp8_attention_a100 batch=1 seq=8 -> 6.2ms
kernel: int8_attention_a100 batch=1 seq=8 -> 9.8ms
kernel: int8_attention_a100 batch=8 seq=128 -> 12.4ms
kernel: fp8_attention_a100 batch=8 seq=128 -> 19.1ms
```

Samir: So FP8 wins on tiny seqs, INT8 wins on large batch/long seq. Our runtime was picking INT8 globally for the model so short seq traffic degraded.

Lee: That explains p95. We need a multidimensional kernel selection policy (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, batch_bucket, hardware).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered: canary_group=5% -> 2026-05-03T14:12Z

Tariq: For KV cache: we should namespace keys with model_variant + quant_config checksum. That prevents cross-variant pollution and avoids corrupted meta. Also consider increasing cache size for canary to prevent eviction spikes while we tune.

Samir: Plan proposal: 1) add model_variant tag to KV cache key (short-term hotfix). 2) add seq_len/batch-aware kernel selection matrix (use offline perf grid to pick kernel per (seq_bucket,batch_bucket)). 3) telemetry: emit kernel_choice and cache_hit by request to analyze distribution. 4) staged rollout with traffic mirroring to canary so we can profile without affecting tail.

Jen: +1. For calibration: are we using per-layer minmax calibration or kl-based? Per-layer sensitivity needs different thresholds.

Samir: We're doing KL-based calibration on representative prompts but only one global threshold. I propose per-layer sensitivity table: variance metric + accepted_local_rmse -> decide quant at layer granularity. We'll exclude any layer with sensitivity > threshold.

Alex: Can you show sample quant config we're deploying?

Samir: Example config we used for canary:

```json
{
  "model": "llama-v2-13b",
  "quantization": {
    "default": "int8",
    "exclude": ["tok_embeddings","lm_head"],
    "per_layer_thresholds": "auto-kl-0.01",
    "calibration_prompts": "s3://redwood/quant/calib/llama-v2-13b/"
  },
  "rollout": {"canary_pct": 5}
}
```

Samir: Need to change to explicit per-layer map once we run sensitivity.

Morgan: Also consider soft-fallback: if kernel_choice increases tail beyond X ms for seq_bucket Y, fallback to FP16/FP8 for that bucket for a minute and emit incident. Helps graceful degradation.

Tariq: One more KV detail: when we quantize weights, cache values (KV tensors) might have different layout/packing. We must version the cache serialization format or store raw unquantized KV alongside quantization metadata. Right now variant-tagging would avoid mixing but we should still be explicit in the cache format.

Samir: Good catch. Add serialization version and quant_checksum to cache metadata.

infra-bot: Perf tests scheduled: a100-xlarge grid run queued (job id: perf-llama13b-1771-01). ETA ~2h.

Alex: Who's owning: implement kernel selector matrix (Lee), KV cache key + serialization bump (Tariq), telemetry and soft-fallback (Jen). Samir will coordinate canary mirroring and re-run calibration.

Lee: I'll prototype selector using 3 seq_buckets: tiny(<32), med(32-128), large(>128) and batch_buckets: s(1), m(2-8), l(>8). We'll pick kernel by minimizing expected p95 from perf grid.

Samir: Great. After infra job returns we'll re-run canary with updated selector + cache fixes. If tail improves we proceed with gradual rollout.

Jen: Also add an alert rule: kernel_choice_tail_pct > 10% -> rollback auto.

Samir: Thanks all. I'll update the rollout doc and post link when ready. :thumbsup:
